task: Simulate News Impact Curves (NIC) across all 10 models inside the Model Confidence Set (MCS) using return shocks defined strictly as 100 * log(Close/Open) in percentage points (-5% to +5% in steps of 1%). Save the plot to imgs/data_properties/mcs_news_impact_curve.png and table to imgs/data_properties/mcs_news_impact_curve.csv. Update Section 6.5 of ref/final_report/thesis_structure.tex to include Figure 6.25 (fig:data-property-nic) and its economic/architectural discussion immediately after Figure 6.24. Recompile the thesis PDF with two passes of pdflatex -synctex=1 from ref/final_report/. Add engle1993 to the bibliography and ref/thesis/references.md, and notes to ref/thesis/thesis_notes.md. Add unit tests in data/tests/test_plot_news_impact_curve.py.
sources: Engle & Ng (1993), Measuring and testing the impact of news on volatility, Journal of Finance, 48(5), 1749-1778
Liu et al. (2023), Global neural networks and the data scaling effect in financial time series forecasting, arXiv:2309.02072 Section 4.3.1
